_note: Procedural settlement sprawl (owner decisions 2026-10-04, game-design §12.13 A and B; docs/map-pipeline-design.md Addendum A; map/sprawl.gd). Presentation only: no gameplay value comes from here. Distances in metres at campaign scale (lords about 8.8 m tall). Per type and level (index 0 = level 1): wall: wall ring radius (0 = none); wall_rings: 2 for double walls; towers_every: wall segments between towers; districts: house rings inside the walls; house_gap: spacing along a ring; suburb: suburbs reach this radius along the roads; villages: outlying villages; village_radius: their distance; farm: farm belt reaches this radius; roads: converging roads (and gates). A level-3 city is about 100 m across, about three times Lothern's footprint in the TW:WH3 reference at the same lord size.

piece_size._note: Footprint (m) each piece is spaced by, per role.

footprint._note: No-overlap rule (owner, 2026-10-06): every settlement owns a circle of radius[type] (its sprawl, walls, suburbs, villages, farms and industry props at max level, measured over every culture and specialization; tests/test_footprints.gd keeps the sprawl inside it) plus a countryside ring, so open country, farms and roads separate one settlement from the next. map/validator.gd fails when two settlements' circles (radius + countryside) touch.

chains._note: Countryside features per building chain, multiplied by the building's level. fields: extra farm fields; mine: mine + spoil heaps + pits + carts in hills (searched up to search metres from the settlement); docks: docks and ships on the nearest coast; yards: tents and fences near the gates; shrines: shrine pillars; stalls/carts: market stalls in the plaza and carts on the roads; towers: extra wall towers; watch: watchtowers on the outer ring; houses: denser districts.

_lod_bias_note: GeometryInstance3D.lod_bias for city MultiMeshes: Godot picks a MultiMesh's LOD from the nearest point of its bounds (a whole city), so without a bias a city near the camera draws every far house at full detail.

detail_ranges._note: Camera distance (m) beyond which a city stops drawing small props (the no_shadow pieces) and houses; walls, towers, keeps and temples draw to the build radius. Keeps far cities cheap; the haze hides the difference.

_no_shadow_note: Pieces drawn without casting shadows (flat or small at campaign scale; fewer shadow draw calls).

colors._note: Farm field patchwork (instance colours of kit.field) and roads.
